fields.Frequency: Quarterly review; new category as needed
fields.Trigger: Annual review or new category launch

Automation Opportunity: - Pricing auto-suggested from the historical claim-rate + repair-cost data; RA 7394-compliance auto-checked
Controls: - CTL-390 (ensure controlled execution — Extended Warranty & Service Contract Management (PA-53.3).)
- CTL-390: extended-warranty pricing adequacy — links to VS-157; service-contract terms conform to the Consumer Act (RA 7394) — links to VS-22; operational: VP Merchandising sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pricing-inadequacy risk**: the claim rate exceeds the pricing assumption, making the product unprofitable; mitigated by the annual re-pricing and the claim-rate monitoring (W2136)
- **RA 7394-non-compliance risk**: the contract terms don't meet the Consumer Act (e.g., unfair exclusion clauses); mitigated by the Legal review in step 2
System Touchpoints: - Item/warranty master (links to VS-29 / W296 service-item master, W2122 warranty config) — the extended-warranty SKU
- Pricing (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-57 / W2232) — the pricing model (claim rate + repair cost + margin)
- Legal/compliance (links to VS-22 / W22.1, VS-88) — the RA 7394 contract-terms review
Time Estimate: ~3.5 days/review × 4 + per-category = **~120 hours/year** Category Manager + Finance + Legal.

steps.activity: Category Manager identifies eligible categories; Finance calculates pricing based on claim rate, repair cost, target margin (40–60%)
Legal reviews contract terms for Consumer Act compliance; Manager configures in ERP with service SKU, pricing tiers, POS upsell rules

fields.Trigger: Customer purchases eligible item at POS

Automation Opportunity: - Prompt auto-displayed; acceptance auto-registered; attach-rate auto-tracked
Controls: - CTL-390 (ensure controlled execution — Extended Warranty & Service Contract Management (PA-53.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer-annoyance risk**: the upsell prompt frustrates customers who don't want it; mitigated by the no-repeated-offers rule and the brief trained script
- **Low-attach-rate risk**: the attach rate is below the 15–20% target; mitigated by the script training and the incentive (links to VS-19 / W228 sales commission)
System Touchpoints: - POS / upsell (links to VS-08 / W5B, POS-013, VS-10 / W794 ecommerce upsell) — the auto-prompt and acceptance
- CRM (links to VS-13 / W17, VS-53 / W2118) — the auto-registration
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the attach-rate and decline-rate tracking
Time Estimate: ~45 sec/transaction × ~42,000/month ≈ ~1,890,000 sec ≈ **~525 hours/month Cashier** (absorbed into checkout, ~30 sec incremental).

steps.activity: POS auto-prompts with warranty options and price; cashier presents offer using trained script
Customer accepts: warranty added to transaction, contract printed on receipt, digital acknowledgment signed; auto-registered in CRM
Customer declines: recorded for analytics; no repeated offers to protect customer experience

fields.Participants: Finance, Finance Manager, Warranty Admin, VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - Liability accrual auto-generated monthly; portfolio-metrics auto-computed quarterly
Controls: - CTL-390: PFRS 15 deferred-revenue accuracy — links to VS-157; CTL-44 (contract-count integrity); operational: Finance Manager monthly sign-off; VP Merchandising quarterly sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Liability-accrual-inaccuracy risk**: the PFRS 15 deferred-revenue accrual doesn't match the actual revenue-recognition pattern (straight-line vs. claims-weighted); mitigated by the quarterly review and the methodology calibration
- **Portfolio-loss risk**: the claim-rate-vs-estimate divergence across the portfolio makes the program unprofitable; mitigated by the quarterly review and the re-pricing
System Touchpoints: - Warranty contract/liability (links to VS-17 / W28, VS-157 / PFRS 15, VS-54 / W2156 breakage pattern) — the deferred-revenue/liability accrual
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the portfolio review dataset
- Pricing (links to VS-53 / W2134) — the annual re-pricing input
Time Estimate: ~5 hours/month + ~5 hours/quarter = **~80 hours/year** Warranty Administrator + Finance.

steps.activity: System maintains contract lifecycle (active/approaching expiry/expired/cancelled); monthly liability accrual journal generated
Quarterly: review contract portfolio (renewal rate, claim rate vs. estimate, cancellation rate, revenue vs. cost); annual re-pricing

fields.Trigger: Customer files claim on product covered by extended warranty

Automation Opportunity: - Contract auto-verified; coverage auto-checked against the contract terms; claim-cost auto-tracked vs. accrual
Controls: - CTL-390 (ensure controlled execution — Extended Warranty & Service Contract Management (PA-53.3).)
- operational: CS Director sign-off; Finance Manager accrual review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coverage-dispute risk**: the customer believes the claim is covered but the contract excludes it (wear, accidental); mitigated by the clear coverage-scope documentation at sale and the Specialist's evidence-based validation
- **Accrual-depletion risk**: the claim cost exceeds the accrued revenue for the contract, making it a loss; mitigated by the quarterly portfolio review (W2136) and the re-pricing
System Touchpoints: - Warranty contract (links to VS-53 / W2136) — the active-contract verification
- Claim system (links to VS-53 / W2126–W2131) — the claim processing
- Finance/accrual (links to VS-17 / W28, VS-157) — the claim-cost-vs-accrual tracking

steps.activity: System verifies active contract, coverage period, claim type; Specialist validates defect is covered (not wear/misuse/accidental)
Specialist authorizes: repair at service center, replacement (>70% of replacement cost), or store credit; Finance tracks vs. accrual

Automation Opportunity: - Renewal notices auto-sent at 90/30/7; contract auto-extended on payment
Controls: - CTL-390 (ensure controlled execution — Extended Warranty & Service Contract Management (PA-53.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Renewal-fatigue risk**: too many renewal notices annoy the customer; mitigated by the 3-touch cadence (90/30/7) and the easy-renewal-link
- **Low-renewal-rate risk**: the renewal rate is below the 25–30% target; mitigated by the pricing (renewal priced attractively) and the multi-channel ease
System Touchpoints: - Warranty contract lifecycle (links to VS-53 / W2136) — the renewal/extension
- Customer comms (links to VS-75 app, VS-10 email) — the renewal notices
- Payment (links to VS-08 / W5B, VS-16 / W8) — the renewal payment
Time Estimate: Automated + ~12 min/phone-renewal × ~700/month = **~140 hours/month** CSR + Warranty Admin (phone subset).

steps.activity: System auto-sends renewal notices at 90, 30, and 7 days with pricing and easy renewal link (online/in-store/phone)
Customer renews via online payment, in-store, or phone; system extends contract, generates new certificate, schedules next expiry cycle

fields.Participants: CSR, CS Supervisor, Finance, Finance Manager

Automation Opportunity: - Proration auto-calculated; refund auto-processed; accrual auto-adjusted
Controls: - CTL-390 (ensure controlled execution — Extended Warranty & Service Contract Management (PA-53.3).)
- operational: CS Supervisor sign-off; Finance Manager accrual-adjustment sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Proration-dispute risk**: the customer disputes the prorated refund (expected full refund after the cooling-off); mitigated by the proration-policy disclosed at sale

- **Refund-abuse risk**: a customer cancels after a large claim, getting a prorated refund despite the claim cost exceeding the premium; mitigated by the proration-minus-claims formula (the refund deducts claims paid)
System Touchpoints: - Warranty contract (links to VS-53 / W2136) — the contract termination
- Refund (links to VS-16 / W101, VS-17 / W9) — the refund processing
- Liability/accrual (links to VS-17 / W28, VS-157) — the accrual adjustment

steps.activity: CSR verifies contract; within 30-day cooling-off: full refund; after: prorated (remaining months / total × price minus claims)
System processes refund to original payment method; terminates contract; adjusts warranty liability accrual; posts GL entries

fields.Participants: Technical Specialist, Category Manager, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Customer invokes building material performance guarantee

Automation Opportunity: - Claim auto-routed to Technical Specialist; site-inspection report auto-templated; vendor-recovery auto-initiated on product-defect finding
Controls: - CTL-390 (ensure controlled execution — Extended Warranty & Service Contract Management (PA-53.3).)
- operational: Category Manager sign-off on claims >PHP 50K
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attribution-dispute risk**: the customer attributes the failure to the product (guarantee claim) but the root cause is installation error (not covered); mitigated by the Technical Specialist's site inspection and the evidence-based attribution

- **High-cost-claim risk**: a full-house repaint or re-tile is a high-value claim that strains the guarantee reserve; mitigated by the vendor-cost-recovery (the manufacturer funds the material) and the insurance partner (W2141)
System Touchpoints: - Guarantee claim (links to VS-53 / W2126 claim system, VS-31 / W110 quality) — the claim record and quality data
- Vendor recovery (links to VS-53 / W2128 vendor escalation, VS-03 / W88 RTV) — the vendor cost-recovery
- Installation/contractor (links to VS-12 / W12 installation services, VS-172 contractor network) — the installation-error assessment
Time Estimate: ~3 hours/site-inspection + ~1.5 days report + ~10 days resolution × ~650/month = **~2,000 hours/month** Technical Specialist + Category Manager (distributed).

steps.activity: Technical Specialist dispatched to customer site: inspects conditions, takes samples/photos, assesses product defect vs. installation error vs. environmental
Specialist submits report: product defect → full claim (material + labor); installation error → deny; mixed cause → partial coverage
For approved claims: processes material replacement and coordinates re-application; vendor notified for cost recovery

fields.Participants: Finance Controller, CFO, Insurance Partner, Legal, CEO
fields.Trigger: Annual contract renewal or quarterly review

Automation Opportunity: - Program financials auto-assembled; loss-ratio auto-computed; partner-performance auto-scored
Controls: - CTL-390: insurance-program accuracy — links to VS-26; CTL-37 (partner-claim integrity); operational: CFO quarterly sign-off; CEO annual strategy sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Self-insure-vs-partner-misjudgment risk**: BuildRight self-insures a category that turns out to have high claim rates (more expensive than a partner premium); mitigated by the quarterly loss-ratio review and the flexibility to switch
- **Partner-approval-rate risk**: the insurance partner denies too many claims, eroding customer satisfaction; mitigated by the quarterly performance review and the approval-rate SLA
System Touchpoints: - Insurance (links to VS-26 / W59 insurance policy lifecycle, W610 claims) — the warranty-insurance partner
- Finance (links to VS-17 / W26 budget, VS-158 / W85) — the program financials
- Vendor scorecard (links to VS-67 / W2458) — the partner-performance review
Time Estimate: ~5 hours/quarter + ~3 days/year ≈ 20 + 24 hours = **~45 hours/year** VP Merchandising + Finance + Legal.

steps.activity: Finance reviews program financials: premium vs. claims recovered, loss ratio, admin costs; determines self-insure vs. partner by category
VP Merchandising conducts quarterly performance review with partner: claim approval rate, turnaround, customer satisfaction, loss ratio
Annual: contract renewal negotiation; Legal reviews terms; VP presents strategy to Executive Committee
